stem: \(\Delta SHR \sim \Delta SVU\), in \(\Delta SHR\), \(SH = 4.5\) cm, \(HR = 5.2\) cm, \(SR = 5.8\) cm and \(\dfrac{SH}{SV} = \dfrac{3}{5}\), Construct \(\Delta SVU\).
solution:
Steps of construction:

1. Draw \(SH = 4.5\) cm.
2. With \(S\) as centre and radius \(5.8\) cm, draw an arc above \(SH\).
3. With \(H\) as centre and radius \(5.2\) cm, draw an arc cutting the previous arc; name the point of intersection \(R\).
4. Join \(SR\) and \(HR\). \(\Delta SHR\) with the given measurements is constructed. Extend \(SH\) and \(SR\) further to the right.
5. Draw any ray \(SX\) making an acute angle with \(SH\), on the side opposite to vertex \(R\).
6. Since \(\dfrac{SH}{SV} = \dfrac{3}{5}\) and \(5 > 3\), the new triangle is larger, so locate 5 points. Mark \(A_1, A_2, A_3, A_4, A_5\) on \(SX\) such that \(SA_1 = A_1A_2 = A_2A_3 = A_3A_4 = A_4A_5\).
7. Join \(A_3H\), and through \(A_5\) draw a line parallel to \(A_3H\) meeting the extension of \(SH\) at \(V\).
8. Through \(V\) draw a line parallel to \(HR\) meeting the extension of \(SR\) at \(U\).

\(\Delta SVU\) is the required triangle.

Why it works: \(A_3\) is used because \(SH\) corresponds to 3 parts and \(A_5\) because \(SV\) corresponds to 5 parts, so \(\dfrac{SH}{SV} = \dfrac{3}{5}\); the parallel \(VU \parallel HR\) then makes \(\Delta SVU \sim \Delta SHR\) by the Basic Proportionality Theorem, with each side of \(\Delta SVU\) equal to \(\dfrac{5}{3}\) of the corresponding side of \(\Delta SHR\).
